corrections.was: Manarat is 2nd of 5 by income in its local market.
corrections.now: Manarat is 3rd of 6. The Olton Project CIO raised £496,482 in the same financial year (to 31 March 2025) against Manarat's £394,135. It was missed in round 1 and is the single most important finding of this research.
corrections.confidence: Confirmed twice against the Charity Commission register.

corrections.was: Manarat's 61% spend ratio is the lowest of every organisation with real figures.
corrections.now: Manarat is not an outlier. Jami runs 65.8% and The Olton Project 51.7%. Reserve-building is a market norm here; what distinguishes Manarat is that its reserve has no public name.

corrections.was: Deen Central and The Hub are separate organisations.
corrections.now: They are the same organisation - Deen Central operates as The Hub at 5-9 Hermitage Road, Solihull B91 2LL. It also offers bereavement services, which round 1 recorded as absent.

corrections.was: Jami Mosque income £1,933,550 (sum of published components).
corrections.now: £1.90m gross per the register's financial history. The component breakdown sums about £33k higher; the register total is used here.

known_gaps: Direct HTTPS fetching of all sites remains blocked by this environment's egress proxy (403 on CONNECT, re-tested). Page-level detail is drawn from the search index rather than live crawls.
No quantitative SEO data: the connected Ahrefs plan does not cover Site Explorer and the Semrush account has no API units remaining.
Solihull Central Masjid filed a nil return for FYE 2024; real activity is not reflected in its published figures.
Ward-level Muslim population for Sheldon was not obtainable from the search index; borough-level figures are used instead.
Deen Central / The Hub publishes no charity financials. A charity 1154494 (Solihull Health & Education Partnership) shares the Hermitage Road address, but the link to Deen Central is unconfirmed.
A second, older registration - THE OLTON PROJECT, 1138839 - exists alongside the CIO 1183781. The CIO appears to have succeeded it; this is unconfirmed.

market_context.demand_signal: The catchment is growing fast. Muslims were 5.3% of Solihull's population at the 2021 Census, up from 2.5% in 2011 - more than double in a decade. Birmingham overall stands at 29.9%, up 8.0 points from 21.8% in 2011, the largest rise of any religious group in the city.
market_context.supply_response: Manarat opened in 2012 as the first purpose-established masjid for Sheldon and Solihull. At least five organisations now serve the same Solihull catchment: The Olton Project (registered 2019), Solihull Central Masjid (2016), Deen Central / The Hub, Solihull Islamic Education Academy, and Manarat itself.
market_context.implication: Manarat's founding advantage was being first into an underserved area. That advantage has expired. Demand is still growing, but supply has grown faster, and Manarat's income fell 13% in the year to 31 March 2025 while a Solihull rival raised more than it did.
market_context.notes: Ward-level religion data for Sheldon was not available; the borough figures above are the reliable ones.

findings.title: Manarat has been overtaken, and did not see it coming
findings.detail: The Olton Project CIO - registered 2019, six years old, in Olton inside Manarat's stated catchment - raised £496,482 in the year to 31 March 2025. Manarat raised £394,135 in the identical financial year, down 13% from £452,950. TOP's core offer is Qur'an and Islamic studies for ages 4-16, running every day of the week, streamed by ability, in small classes, sold through a dedicated academy website. That is Manarat's core programme, positioned better and marketed harder.
findings.evidence: Charity Commission register, both charities, FYE 31 March 2025. Confirmed twice.

findings.title: Income fell for the first time in five years
findings.detail: Income ran £128.9k, £210.1k, £330.4k, £453.0k, then £394.1k - roughly tripling over four years before dropping 13%. Expenditure rose through the decline, from £232.9k to £239.2k. One down year is not a trend, but it is the first, and it happened in the same year a local rival out-raised the organisation.
findings.evidence: Charity Commission financial history, FYE 31 March 2021-2025.

findings.title: The website cannot take a donation
findings.detail: Published routes are cheque and in person. Every direct competitor with a live site except SIEA takes card payments; The Olton Project takes them through JustGiving. Cash-and-cheque giving structurally excludes under-40 donors and makes Ramadan night-giving - the highest-intent moment in the Islamic giving calendar - almost impossible to capture.
findings.evidence: Manarat donation page; competitor donation pages and platform listings.

findings.title: Prayer times are a six-year-old PDF
findings.detail: The timetable on the site was uploaded in July 2020. Prayer times are the highest-frequency reason a local Muslim opens a masjid website, and that recurring traffic currently goes to MosquePay, The Masjid App and MosqueFinder. Jami, Deen Central and GLMCC all host live timetables themselves.

findings.title: £660k has accumulated with no public name on it
findings.detail: Five years of surpluses total roughly £660,600. The 61% spend ratio on its own is not the problem - Jami runs 65.8% and The Olton Project 51.7%, so reserve-building is normal here. The problem is that Manarat's reserve is the only one with no named project attached. GLMCC has the GLMCC Expansion Project; Jami is visibly building property and a school. An unnamed reserve raises nothing and explains nothing.
findings.evidence: Charity Commission financial history 2021-2025; competitor campaign pages.

findings.title: The education offer has no shop window
findings.detail: The Olton Project sells its academy on its own domain; SIEA has a dedicated site. Manarat's three-year Hifz programme, Arabic course and Islamic studies - substantively a stronger offer than either - live inside one undifferentiated /services/ page with no fees, no timetable, no age ranges and no enquiry form. Parents choosing a madrasah cannot compare Manarat without phoning.

findings.title: Single-source income concentration
findings.detail: Manarat appears almost entirely donation-funded and is the only organisation in the set with no earned-income line. Jami takes 19% from donations and carries the rest on rental and school fees; Solihull Central hires out catering equipment; Deen Central hires out rooms; TOP and SIEA charge course fees. Deen Central, donation-only until recently, reported a near-total collapse in donor income while overheads continued.
findings.evidence: Competitor income breakdowns and service listings.

findings.title: The founding advantage has expired
findings.detail: Manarat opened in 2012 as the first purpose-established masjid for Sheldon and Solihull. At least five organisations now serve that catchment. Demand is genuinely growing - Solihull's Muslim population went from 2.5% to 5.3% between the 2011 and 2021 Censuses - but supply has grown faster, and Solihull Central now claims to be the first and only Solihull masjid with a full-time Imam.
findings.evidence: ONS Census 2021; Solihull Central positioning; charity registration dates.

findings.title: No funeral or bereavement service
findings.detail: Jami has run funerals since 1995, GLMCC offers them, and Deen Central runs a bereavement service from a much weaker financial base. A bereaved family that has to go elsewhere at the hardest moment of their lives tends to keep going there afterwards. This is the highest-loyalty service in the sector.

findings.title: No visible women's or youth programme
findings.detail: Jami runs JMIC Muslimah with its own site section; SIEA runs weekly badminton and football; TOP runs coffee mornings, excursions and movie nights. Manarat's public offer - prayers, Quran, Arabic, Nikah - reaches men and children, but not women or teenagers as distinct constituencies.

findings.title: Discoverability is rented, not owned
findings.detail: MosquePay, The Masjid App, MosqueFinder and Giving is Great own the recurring visit and the donor relationship. Fine as acquisition channels; a problem as the primary one. Manarat also has no newsletter, so there is no owned channel to a supporter at all.

findings.title: The strongest differentiator is unstated
findings.detail: Founded by scholars, the first purpose-established masjid for Sheldon and Solihull, and an explicit anti-extremism position. That last one is rare, publicly valuable, and absent from how the site sells itself - while Solihull Central actively markets its full-time Imam.

recommendations.action: Build a proper education shop window - a page per programme (Hifz, Arabic, Islamic studies, Nikah) with fees, timetable, age ranges, teacher credentials and an enquiry form; ideally a dedicated academy section
recommendations.rationale: This is where Manarat is being beaten by an organisation with a weaker offer. It is also the cheapest thing on this list.

recommendations.action: Live prayer timetable - auto-calculated, mobile-first, with Jumu'ah and Janazah announcements
recommendations.rationale: Recovers the highest-frequency reason to visit; every other ask can then sit next to it.

recommendations.action: Native online donation flow with card and Apple/Google Pay, plus Gift Aid capture
recommendations.rationale: Gift Aid is worth 25p per eligible pound and is currently uncollected on cash and cheque. Directly addresses the income decline.

recommendations.action: Name the capital project the £660k reserve is building toward, with its own appeal page and a progress figure
recommendations.rationale: An unnamed reserve raises nothing; a named project raises money and explains the surplus at the same time.

recommendations.action: Recurring monthly giving tier priced as a daily habit
recommendations.rationale: Converts volatile seasonal giving into a predictable base. 200 donors at £15/month is £36k of certainty - and would have absorbed most of this year's £59k decline.

recommendations.action: Start an email newsletter and capture addresses at every touchpoint
recommendations.rationale: Manarat currently has no owned channel to a single supporter. Deen Central, in financial distress, still has one.

recommendations.action: Open a second income line from the existing building - hall hire, the car park, or paid short courses
recommendations.rationale: A 1,000-capacity building with a large car park is an under-used asset, and Manarat is the only organisation in the set with no earned income at all.

recommendations.action: Introduce a funeral and bereavement service
recommendations.rationale: The highest-loyalty service in the sector, and the clearest reason local families currently register with someone else.

recommendations.action: Start a women's programme and a youth activity, each with its own page
recommendations.rationale: Matches JMIC Muslimah, SIEA's sport clubs and TOP's social programme; reaches the constituencies now missed.

recommendations.action: Lead with scholarship - the founding scholars, the Sheldon-Solihull first-mover story, and the anti-extremism position
recommendations.rationale: The one thing no local competitor can copy, and the answer to Solihull Central's full-time-Imam claim.
